algorithm.title: Diagnostic test cutoff thresholds and receiver operating characteristics

nodes.text: Diagnostic test cutoff determines classification of continuous biomarkers
Shifting cutoff threshold shifts distribution of true and false test results
**Raising cutoff threshold (e.g. 5% to 8%):** test is harder to call positive
**Effect on sensitivity:** fewer diseased patients test positive -> decreased sensitivity
**Effect on specificity:** fewer disease-free patients test positive -> increased specificity
**Lowering cutoff threshold:** test is easier to call positive -> increased sensitivity + decreased specificity
Optimize cutoff using ROC curve analysis to balance clinical trade-offs

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

Misfolded protein retained in hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum → cellular injury, fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Serum AAT level** → phenotype or genotype confirmation; acute inflammation can falsely elevate levels
Test all adults with COPD, unexplained bronchiectasis, or unexplained chronic liver disease
Spirometry establishes obstruction; chest CT defines distribution; LFTs and ultrasound assess hepatic injury

IV AAT augmentation for selected nonsmokers with severe deficiency and established emphysema; specialist selection
Augmentation does not treat liver injury; decompensated cirrhosis → liver transplantation
End-stage pulmonary disease despite treatment → lung transplantation evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension, recurrent respiratory infections
Cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma; hepatic cancer surveillance once cirrhosis develops

rows.label: Prevention
items: Offer genetic counseling and testing to first-degree relatives; genotype rather than level alone
Influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal vaccines; hepatitis A/B vaccination with liver disease
Avoid excess alcohol and hepatotoxic exposures; monitor pulmonary function and liver tests

items: Sepsis, pneumonia, aspiration, major trauma, pancreatitis, near-drowning, massive transfusion

★ Ventilate at **6 mL/kg predicted body weight**; plateau pressure ≤30 cm H2O

After shock resolves → conservative fluid strategy; avoid prolonged high-pressure recruitment maneuvers
Consider corticosteroids; early severe dyssynchrony → neuromuscular blockade; refractory severe disease → VV-ECMO evaluation

Critical illness weakness, delirium, persistent exercise limitation; mortality often reflects underlying multiorgan failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: Aspiration precautions, infection prevention, prompt sepsis treatment; avoid unnecessary transfusions
Daily sedation assessment, spontaneous breathing trials when improving, venous thromboembolism prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiogenic edema: elevated filling pressures, LV dysfunction, improvement with decongestion
Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage: falling hemoglobin; progressively bloodier bronchoalveolar lavage
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxemia with relatively clear imaging; CT pulmonary angiography identifies thrombus

carotid-artery-stenosis.name: Carotid artery stenosis
carotid-artery-stenosis.scope: Asymptomatic carotid bruit, carotid duplex ultrasound, medical management, indications for carotid endarterectomy
carotid-artery-stenosis.core: Carotid atherosclerosis causes ipsilateral retinal or cerebral ischemia; intervention depends on symptoms, stenosis severity, and operative risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia; coronary or peripheral arterial disease
Prior neck radiation increases stenosis and surgical complexity

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Amaurosis fugax** (painless curtain-like monocular vision loss), contralateral weakness, aphasia → symptomatic disease
Bruit may be incidental; loudness does not measure severity, complete occlusion may be silent
Isolated dizziness or syncope rarely represents carotid-territory ischemia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Plaque rupture → artery-to-artery emboli; critical narrowing can reduce cerebral perfusion
Retinal **Hollenhorst plaque** (cholesterol embolus) → ulcerated ipsilateral carotid plaque

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected stenosis or selected incidental bruit evaluation → **carotid duplex ultrasound**
CTA/MRA confirms anatomy before intervention; brain imaging evaluates neurologic deficits
★ **No routine screening** of asymptomatic general adults; bruit auscultation is an unreliable screen

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ All: **antiplatelet + high-intensity statin**, BP and diabetes control
Symptomatic operative candidates: endarterectomy generally within **2 weeks**, after neurologic stabilization
Classic asymptomatic CEA criteria: ≥70%, life expectancy ≥3–5 years, perioperative stroke/death <3%; individualized decision
CREST-2: asymptomatic stenting benefited selected patients; CEA lacked significant benefit; avoid automatic surgery
Symptomatic older adults: CEA generally preferred to stenting; high surgical-risk anatomy may favor stenting

rows.label: Complications
items: Ischemic stroke, recurrent TIAs; procedure → stroke, MI, cranial nerve injury
Hyperperfusion after revascularization → headache, seizures, brain hemorrhage; driven by **postoperative hypertension**
New deficit after endarterectomy → **noncontrast head CT** first: hemorrhage vs carotid thrombosis; no heparin/tPA beforehand
★ Expanding neck hematoma with stridor → **open wound/emergent neck exploration**; no imaging delay

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, Mediterranean-style diet; sustained vascular risk reduction
New focal neurologic symptoms → emergency stroke assessment, even after symptom resolution

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic stenosis: cardiac murmur radiates to both carotids
Cardioembolism: atrial fibrillation or cardiac thrombus; multiple vascular territories
Migraine aura: gradually spreading positive visual/sensory symptoms
Giant cell arteritis: headache, jaw claudication, ↑ESR; vision loss often persistent

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.name: Chromosomal and genetic disorders
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.scope: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (45,X0), Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 trinucleotide repeat), Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes, DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion)
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.core: Recognize syndromic combinations of growth, cognition, gonadal function, dysmorphism, and congenital malformations; confirm with the correct genetic test.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced maternal age: meiotic nondisjunction; balanced parental translocation: recurrent aneuploid pregnancy
Family expansion history: repeat disorders; microdeletions often de novo

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Down** (trisomy 21): hypotonia, upslanting fissures, epicanthal folds, macroglossia, single palmar crease, AV septal defect
DiGeorge: conotruncal defect, cleft palate, absent thymus, hypocalcemic tetany
Turner: newborn hand/foot lymphedema, redundant nuchal skin; later nevi
**Williams** (7q11.23 deletion): overfriendly, elfin facies, hyperacusis, intellectual disability, supravalvular stenosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Genomic imprinting**: parent-specific expression; deletion or uniparental disomy can disrupt the active copy
22q11 deletion disrupts pharyngeal pouch development → T-cell deficiency and hypoparathyroidism

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected Down, Turner, Klinefelter → **karyotype**; prenatal screening alone never establishes diagnosis
Microarray: microdeletion; targeted repeat analysis: fragile X; methylation testing: imprinting disorders
Down: assess heart, hearing, vision, thyroid; DiGeorge: calcium and lymphocyte subsets

rows.label: Tx
items: Early developmental services, speech support; repair congenital defects
Turner: growth hormone then estrogen/progestin; Klinefelter: testosterone after endocrine assessment
Prader-Willi: supervised food access; Angelman: seizure management; DiGeorge: calcium and infection management

rows.label: Complications
items: Down: duodenal atresia (double bubble), leukemia, early Alzheimer disease, atlantoaxial instability
Turner: coarctation, bicuspid valve, aortic dissection; Klinefelter: infertility, breast cancer
Prader-Willi: severe obesity; DiGeorge: severe infections and later psychiatric disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Genetic counseling**: recurrence depends on nondisjunction, translocation, imprinting mechanism, or repeat expansion
Avoid live vaccines with severe T-cell deficiency; use irradiated blood for profound immunodeficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Noonan syndrome: Turner-like habitus, normal chromosomes; either sex, pulmonic stenosis
Congenital hypothyroidism: hypotonia and delayed development; abnormal newborn thyroid screen
Constitutional delay: delayed bone age; no edema or nevi
Rett: girls with regression; MECP2 variant

table.title: Distinctive genotype–phenotype pairs
rows: Short female, webbed neck, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea
Tall male, small firm testes, gynecomastia, high FSH/LH
FMR1 CGG expansion at X fragile site; silencing
Long face, large ears, macroorchidism, autism-like behavior
IUGR, clenched overlapping fingers, prominent occiput, micrognathia, VSD

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established genetics teaching.

chronic-kidney-disease.name: Chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease
chronic-kidney-disease.scope: CKD progression, anemia of CKD (erythropoietin deficiency), mineral and bone disorder, uremic complications, volume overload, indications for emergent dialysis (AEIOU), vascular access
chronic-kidney-disease.core: Persistent kidney injury or reduced filtration causes progressive cardiovascular, metabolic and uremic complications; dialysis follows clinical indications rather than creatinine alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, hypertension, glomerular disease, obstruction, recurrent AKI, inherited cystic disease
NSAIDs, smoking and uncontrolled proteinuria accelerate progression

rows.label: Clues
items: Early disease often asymptomatic; advanced disease → fatigue, pruritus, anorexia, edema
Uremia: confusion, myoclonus, pericardial friction rub, nausea or bleeding despite normal platelet count
Labs: normocytic anemia, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, ↑phosphate, low/normal calcium

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nephron loss → hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, proteinuria and fibrosis
↓Erythropoietin → anemia; phosphate retention/↓calcitriol → ↓calcium absorption → four-gland secondary hyperparathyroidism
Renal bone disease: ↓calcitriol → **deficient osteoid mineralization**, atraumatic fracture; ↑PTH → subperiosteal resorption

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **eGFR <60** or kidney-damage markers for **≥3 months** establishes CKD
Urine albumin/creatinine ratio, urinalysis, creatinine trend; ultrasound for size/obstruction
Stage by GFR and albuminuria; small echogenic kidneys support chronicity but are not universal
Monitor CBC, ferritin/TSAT, K, bicarbonate, calcium, phosphate and PTH

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Albuminuric CKD → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**; monitor creatinine/K; never combine both
SGLT2 inhibitor for T2DM or qualifying albuminuric CKD/HF, generally starting eGFR ≥20
Overload → salt restriction, furosemide; high phosphate → phosphorus restriction, sevelamer; severe hyperparathyroidism → calcitriol
Iron repletion before ESA for selected persistent anemia; correct clinically significant metabolic acidosis
★ **Dialysis (AEIOU)**: refractory acidosis/hyperkalemia/overload (anuria: no diuretics), dialyzable toxins, uremic complications

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiovascular death, fractures, severe hyperkalemic arrhythmia, malnutrition
Dialysis access infection/thrombosis; rapid urea reduction → dialysis disequilibrium
Peritoneal dialysis + fever/abdominal pain → first **peritoneal fluid cell count, Gram stain, culture**

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Preserve arm veins; plan **AV fistula** before hemodialysis; temporary catheter for emergencies; early transplant referral
BP/glycemic control, avoid nephrotoxins, renal drug adjustment; hepatitis B vaccination before dialysis

rows.label: Mimics
items: AKI: acute creatinine change; may complicate established CKD
Prerenal azotemia: reversible perfusion deficit without persistent structural injury

cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.name: Cirrhosis and portal hypertension
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.scope: Ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, esophageal varices, hepatorenal syndrome, hepatocellular carcinoma screening
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.core: Cirrhosis produces portal hypertension and synthetic failure; new ascites, bleeding, confusion or kidney injury signals decompensation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Alcohol, chronic HBV/HCV, metabolic steatotic liver disease; autoimmune/cholestatic disorders

rows.label: Clues
items: Splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, spider angiomas, jaundice, muscle wasting
Encephalopathy: **asterixis**; triggers GI bleeding, infection, constipation, sedatives, hypokalemia, protein load
SBP may present only with subtle confusion or renal deterioration; fever/pain can be absent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fibrosis raises intrahepatic resistance; splanchnic vasodilation lowers effective arterial volume
Portal collaterals bleed; impaired toxin clearance causes neuropsychiatric dysfunction
SBP: **intestinal bacterial translocation** into ascitic fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ New/worsening or hospitalized ascites → **diagnostic paracentesis**; PMN **≥250/µL** → treat SBP
SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL supports portal hypertension; send ascitic culture in bedside blood-culture bottles
HRS-AKI: exclude shock, nephrotoxins, obstruction and structural injury; assess volume response
MELD-Na/MELD 3.0 guides prognosis/transplant assessment
Encephalopathy clinical: **ammonia** not diagnostic; older exam questions may expect serum ammonia after normal head CT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Variceal bleed → resuscitate, **octreotide + ceftriaxone**, urgent endoscopic banding; refractory → TIPS
Ascites → sodium restriction, spironolactone ± furosemide; tense ascites → paracentesis, albumin if >5 L
★ SBP → **ceftriaxone**, albumin for high-risk renal/liver dysfunction; reassess response
Encephalopathy → lactulose to 2–3 soft stools/day, rifaximin (add for recurrence); correct trigger; no sedatives
HRS → stop diuretics/nephrotoxins, **terlipressin + albumin** after volume assessment; monitor hypoxia; transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: HCC, recurrent infection, malnutrition, hepatopulmonary syndrome; TIPS can worsen encephalopathy
Avoid NSAIDs, sedatives and unnecessary fluid loading; INR alone poorly predicts procedural bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Ultrasound + AFP every 6 months** for HCC surveillance in eligible cirrhosis
Carvedilol for clinically significant portal hypertension when tolerated; banding if indicated and beta blocker unsuitable
After SBP → antibiotic prophylaxis; alcohol abstinence, hepatitis vaccines, adequate protein intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiac ascites: high SAAG with ascitic protein ≥2.5 g/dL
Malignant/TB ascites: usually low SAAG

contact-dermatitis.name: Contact dermatitis
contact-dermatitis.scope: Allergic contact dermatitis (poison ivy/urushiol, nickel, neomycin, type IV hypersensitivity), irritant contact dermatitis, patch testing, topical corticosteroids, allergen avoidance
contact-dermatitis.core: Pruritic eczema confined to an exposure pattern; delayed allergy or direct chemical injury, sometimes spreading beyond contact sites.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Allergens: urushiol, nickel jewelry, fragrances, latex additives, neomycin, occupational chemicals
Irritants: repeated handwashing, detergents, solvents, prolonged wet work; atopic skin increases susceptibility
Repeated surgeries, healthcare work → **latex sensitization**

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Linear vesicles** after outdoor exposure; geometric plaques under jewelry, adhesive, or topical products
Acute: erythema, edema, weeping; chronic: fissuring, scaling, lichenification
Irritant disease often burns or stings; allergic disease usually itches
Extensive blistering, facial swelling, genital involvement → assess severity and secondary infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergic: sensitized T cells mediate **type IV hypersensitivity**; symptoms 24–72 hours after re-exposure
Irritant: direct epidermal barrier damage; no prior sensitization required

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical exposure history and distribution first; review work, hobbies, cosmetics, and new skin products
Persistent or unclear allergic disease → **patch testing**, read after delayed intervals
Skin-prick testing and serum IgE do not diagnose delayed contact allergy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Remove exposure → emollients and **topical corticosteroids**; choose potency by body site
Face, groin, folds: low-potency hydrocortisone; thick extremity plaques: triamcinolone
★ Poison ivy **>20% BSA** or severe face/genital disease → oral prednisone taper **2–3 weeks**
Cool wet compresses for oozing; antibiotics only for bacterial superinfection

rows.label: Complications
items: Excoriation → impetigo; persistent exposure → chronic hand eczema and work disability
Prolonged potent topical steroids → skin atrophy, striae; systemic steroids → hyperglycemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protective gloves and barrier care; fragrance-free products; avoid the identified allergen
Wash urushiol promptly from skin, clothing, and tools; blister fluid does not spread dermatitis
Hand eczema ± generalized urticaria → latex allergy: **strict avoidance**, including intraoperatively; no desensitization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atopic dermatitis: chronic flexural eczema, personal or family atopy
Tinea: advancing annular scaly border; KOH reveals hyphae
Scabies: nocturnal itch, finger-web burrows, affected close contacts

contact-dermatitis.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatology teaching.

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.scope: Stable COPD, acute exacerbation (AECOPD), oxygen-induced hypercapnia, noninvasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP), indications for intubation, bronchodilators and glucocorticoids
copd.core: Persistent airflow obstruction after inhalational exposure causes progressive exertional dyspnea and episodic infectious or inflammatory exacerbations.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dusts; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early/basilar emphysema

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic cough/sputum, prolonged expiration, wheeze, hyperinflation
★ **Somnolence, exhaustion, silent chest, worsening acidosis** → impending respiratory failure
Exacerbation: ↑dyspnea, purulent sputum, rhonchi, **no infiltrate** → acute bronchitis, not pneumonia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-airway inflammation + alveolar destruction → expiratory collapse, air trapping, impaired diffusion
Excess oxygen worsens CO₂ retention mainly through V/Q mismatch and Haldane effect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Postbronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.70** confirms persistent obstruction in compatible clinical setting
Exacerbation: pulse oximetry; ABG for severe distress/altered mentation; radiograph for pneumonia, edema, pneumothorax
Consider ECG, troponin, BNP, or PE evaluation when symptoms exceed expected exacerbation pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **albuterol + ipratropium**, prednisone for 5 days; titrate oxygen to 88–92%
Antibiotics: purulence + increased dyspnea/sputum volume, or ventilatory support; doxycycline/azithromycin options
★ Hypercapnic acidosis, pH ≤7.35 → **BiPAP** unless aspiration risk, arrest, instability, inability to cooperate
Intubate for failed NIV, severe encephalopathy, refractory hypoxemia, or inability to protect airway
Long-term oxygen if stable PaO₂ ≤55 or saturation ≤88%; selected cor pulmonale/polycythemia with PaO₂ 56–59

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, secondary polycythemia, cachexia
Pneumonia risk with inhaled steroids; ventilation → dynamic hyperinflation, auto-PEEP, barotrauma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**, influenza/COVID/pneumococcal/RSV vaccination when eligible, pulmonary rehabilitation
Check inhaler technique/adherence; offer alpha-1 antitrypsin testing at least once

rows.label: Mimics
items: Asthma: variable symptoms and reversible obstruction
Heart failure: orthopnea, edema, vascular congestion; bronchiectasis: copious sputum, dilated bronchi

table.title: Stable inhaled treatment
rows: Exacerbations with eosinophilia or concurrent asthma

copd.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [GOLD 2026](https://goldcopd.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GOLD-REPORT-2026-v1.3-8Dec2025_WMV2.pdf); acute ventilatory care: established teaching.

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative
False negatives → low sensitivity, an intrinsic test property; NPV varies with prevalence

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in; LR− <0.1 rules out; **LR 1** → no information

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect
ROC point nearest **upper-left corner** → best combined sensitivity and specificity

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage
Older adults: large-artery stiffness (low compliance) → **isolated systolic hypertension**, wide pulse pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance
Child/adolescent high oscillometric reading → **confirm by auscultation** before ambulatory monitoring or workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB (older exams: any diabetes)
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults
Weight loss: largest lifestyle BP drop, ~1 mm Hg/kg; smoking cessation barely lowers resting BP
BP control: largest modifiable stroke-risk reduction; also prevents concentric LVH and HF

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.scope: Clinical diagnosis, empiric PPI trial, lifestyle measures, alarm symptoms, Barrett esophagus screening, 24-hour pH monitoring
gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.core: Heartburn and acid regurgitation after meals or recumbency suggest reflux; complications or diagnostic uncertainty change the testing pathway.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, pregnancy, hiatal hernia, smoking; drugs reducing lower esophageal sphincter tone
Late large meals and individual food triggers exacerbate symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Sour taste, nocturnal symptoms, chest discomfort; chronic nocturnal/supine cough may be sole symptom
★ **Dysphagia, odynophagia, bleeding, weight loss**, persistent vomiting, anemia → endoscopy
Exertional chest pain → cardiac evaluation; nocturnal burning relieved upright → empiric acid suppression
Infant spit-up + **poor weight gain** → pathologic GERD; pyloric stenosis: projectile vomiting at 3–6 weeks

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transient lower sphincter relaxation and impaired barrier allow gastric contents into esophagus
Acid exposure → erosions; chronic injury may produce intestinal metaplasia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms without alarms → **8-week empiric once-daily PPI trial**
Alarm features or failed treatment → upper endoscopy; biopsies evaluate alternative mucosal disease
★ Unproven GERD + normal endoscopy → **ambulatory pH monitoring off PPI**
Proven GERD with refractory symptoms → impedance-pH testing on PPI after optimizing use
Manometry evaluates motility and precedes antireflux surgery; not the primary reflux diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Omeprazole 30–60 minutes before breakfast**; verify adherence before escalation
Intermittent mild symptoms → antacid or famotidine; persistent breakthrough → optimize/split PPI schedule
Weight reduction if overweight; avoid meals within 2–3 hours of bedtime, elevate bed head
Objective reflux with regurgitation or **recurrent aspiration** despite drugs → fundoplication; gastrostomy alone inadequate
Severe erosive esophagitis → long-term PPI or surgery; step down uncomplicated controlled disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Erosive esophagitis, peptic stricture, Barrett esophagus, adenocarcinoma
Stricture → **endoscopy + biopsy to exclude cancer**, then dilation plus acid suppression
Barrett dysplasia → endoscopic eradication; low-grade, older questions: EGD/biopsy at 6 months, even after fundoplication

rows.label: Prevention
items: Barrett screening: chronic reflux + ≥3 additional risks: male, >50, White, tobacco, obesity, first-degree family history
Smoking cessation and symptom-directed trigger reduction; routine endoscopy unnecessary for every reflux patient

rows.label: Mimics
items: Achalasia: solids and liquids dysphagia, impaired sphincter relaxation
Eosinophilic esophagitis: atopy, food impaction, eosinophilic biopsy
Functional heartburn: normal reflux burden and no symptom association

gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established ACG reflux and Barrett screening teaching.

gastrointestinal-bleeding.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
gastrointestinal-bleeding.scope: Upper GI bleeding (PUD, varices, Mallory-Weiss), lower GI bleeding (diverticular, angiodysplasia, hemorrhoids), fluid and transfusion thresholds, endoscopy
gastrointestinal-bleeding.core: Hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia → assess hemodynamics before localizing; brisk upper bleeding can present as bright red rectal blood.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: NSAIDs/H pylori → ulcers; cirrhosis → varices; forceful retching → mucosal tear
Anticoagulants/antiplatelets increase severity; older age favors diverticula or angiodysplasia

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Syncope, orthostasis, shock** signal major loss; initial hemoglobin may remain normal
Epigastric pain supports ulcer; painless bleeding favors vascular sources
Recurrent occult loss → iron deficiency
**Melena**, elevated BUN/creatinine ratio → upper source; bilious NG aspirate argues against upper bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosal injury, portal-pressure collaterals, or fragile vessels rupture into GI lumen
Volume depletion → reduced perfusion; ongoing bleeding may require massive transfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Two large-bore IVs, CBC, type/cross, coagulation tests**, serial hemoglobin; resuscitate before procedures
Upper source → EGD within 24 hours after stabilization; suspected varices → within 12 hours
★ Ongoing hemodynamically significant hematochezia → **CT angiography → embolization** if active extravasation
Stable lower bleeding → bowel preparation and nonemergent colonoscopy; routine <24-hour colonoscopy adds no benefit
Rectal bleeding mixed with stool, age ≥45 → colonoscopy; negative FOBT does not exclude neoplasia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crystalloid initially; stable nonischemic adults → **RBC transfusion at hemoglobin <7 g/dL**
Exsanguination or post-crystalloid shock → **RBCs** regardless of hemoglobin, not vasopressors; cardiac ischemia → higher threshold
Severe anticoagulant bleeding → drug-specific reversal; uncontrolled varices → balloon tamponade as temporary bridge only
Failed endoscopy → IR/surgery; massive unlocalized lower bleeding → **total abdominal colectomy**, not segmental
Suspected ulcer → IV PPI; endoscopic hemostasis for active bleeding/visible vessel, then high-dose PPI

rows.label: Complications
items: Rebleeding, aspiration, myocardial ischemia, AKI; variceal bleeding → infection
Massive transfusion → hypocalcemia, hypothermia, coagulopathy; embolization → bowel ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Eradicate H pylori and confirm cure; avoid NSAIDs; PPI for high-risk users
After variceal control: nonselective beta-blocker plus repeat banding; recurrent bleeding → TIPS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron/bismuth: dark stool without blood loss
Hemoptysis: coughing frothy blood rather than vomiting
Swallowed epistaxis: nasal source on examination

table.title: Source-specific branches
rows: Postretching tear; Boerhaave instead: chest pain, crepitus
Liver trauma + jaundice; blood from ampulla
