heart-failure.name: Heart failure
heart-failure.scope: HFrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema, guideline-directed medical therapy, neurohormonal activation (RAAS, ADH-mediated hyponatremia)
heart-failure.core: Inadequate cardiac output or elevated filling pressures → pulmonary or systemic congestion, even with a normal ejection fraction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CAD, hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy
Decompensation triggers: ischemia, infection, arrhythmia, missed diuretics, NSAIDs

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, elevated JVP, crackles or wheeze (cardiac asthma), dependent edema
S3 suggests volume overload; S4 suggests stiff ventricle
★ **Flash edema**: abrupt respiratory distress, severe hypertension, pink frothy sputum

rows.label: Pathophys
items: RAAS/sympathetic activation → vasoconstriction, sodium retention, adverse remodeling
Low effective volume → baroreceptor-driven nonosmotic **ADH** release → dilutional hyponatremia; marker of advanced disease
Alveolar flooding → V/Q mismatch, widened A-a gradient, hypoxemia
High-output HF: severe anemia, AV fistula (larger fistula → more shunt); HF signs with **normal/high EF**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography**: EF, valves, wall motion; ECG, CXR, BNP support diagnosis
Low BNP argues against HF; obesity lowers BNP, renal dysfunction raises it
Identify precipitant: troponin, CBC, electrolytes, creatinine; evaluate ischemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute congestion → **IV furosemide**; hypoxemia → oxygen; respiratory distress → noninvasive ventilation
★ Hypertensive pulmonary edema → **IV nitroglycerin**; shock → norepinephrine ± dobutamine, urgent cause correction
Congested HFrEF → loop diuretic + **ACE inhibitor/ARNI first**; beta-blocker/MRA once compensated; ACE inhibitor → ARNI: 36-hour washout
MRA: eGFR >30, K <5; never ACE inhibitor + ARB; EF ≤35% despite GDMT → consider ICD
HFrEF foundation drugs lower mortality; loop diuretics, nitrates alone, digoxin relieve symptoms only

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiorenal syndrome, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, hepatic congestion
Diuresis → hypokalemia; RAAS blockade → hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; monitor creatinine/K

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily weights, sodium moderation, adherence; **continue GDMT after EF recovery**
Treat hypertension, CAD, AF; smoking cessation, exercise, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: COPD: obstructive spirometry, hyperinflation
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia
PE: pleuritic pain, thrombotic risk, RV strain
ARDS: diffuse infiltrates, no cephalization; massive crystalloid + **cephalization/perihilar fullness** → volume overload

table.title: Chronic phenotypes
rows: Sacubitril/valsartan (or ACEi/ARB), carvedilol/metoprolol succinate, spironolactone, dapagliflozin

heart-failure.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC HFrEF 2024](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/03/06/19/22/2024-acc-expert-consensus-hfref); other points established teaching.

herpes-zoster.name: Herpes zoster
herpes-zoster.scope: Varicella zoster reactivation, dermatomal rash, herpes zoster ophthalmicus, Ramsay Hunt syndrome, oral antivirals, postherpetic neuralgia, Shingrix vaccine
herpes-zoster.core: Latent varicella-zoster reactivation causes painful unilateral dermatomal vesicles; ophthalmic involvement or disseminated disease changes urgency and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, HIV, malignancy, transplantation, immunosuppressive drugs
Previous chickenpox or live varicella vaccination establishes latency; no new exposure required

rows.label: Clues
items: Burning/allodynia can precede eruption by days; crops crust over approximately 7–10 days
★ **V1 distribution, nasal-tip lesions, eye pain** → urgent ophthalmology for zoster ophthalmicus
★ **Ear vesicles + ipsilateral facial paralysis** ± hearing/vestibular symptoms → Ramsay Hunt syndrome
Multiple noncontiguous dermatomes or >20 lesions outside primary/adjacent dermatomes suggests dissemination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced VZV-specific cellular immunity permits virus to travel from sensory ganglion to skin
Neuronal inflammation/injury explains acute pain and persistent neuropathic symptoms

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical eruption → **clinical diagnosis**; atypical lesions → vesicle-base VZV PCR
Assess ocular, neurologic, and systemic findings; consider immunodeficiency evaluation for unusually severe/recurrent disease
CSF PCR for suspected CNS infection; do not delay treatment in high-risk presentations

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Valacyclovir, famciclovir, or acyclovir** ideally within 72 hours; still treat new lesions or complications
Dissemination, visceral/CNS disease, severe immunosuppression → **IV acyclovir**
Acute pain: acetaminophen/NSAID, add neuropathic agent when needed; avoid routine systemic steroids
Ramsay Hunt: antiviral plus glucocorticoid early; eye lubrication/protection for incomplete closure
Postherpetic neuralgia: **gabapentin**/pregabalin, lidocaine patch; TCA anticholinergic in elderly; no late antiviral

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent pain >90 days, secondary bacterial infection, corneal injury, vision loss
Meningoencephalitis, vasculopathy, visceral spread in vulnerable patients

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Shingrix two doses** for adults ≥50 years or immunocompromised ≥19 years, including prior zoster
Cover lesions, **avoid susceptible contacts** until crusted; exposure causes chickenpox, not immediate shingles
Disseminated: airborne/contact until crusted; immunocompromised localized: same precautions until dissemination excluded

rows.label: Mimics
items: HSV: recurrent localized lesions, often oral/genital rather than a full dermatome
Contact dermatitis: prominent itch, exposure pattern, no neuropathic prodrome

hypercalcemia.name: Hypercalcemia
hypercalcemia.scope: Primary hyperparathyroidism, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, milk-alkali syndrome, IV saline resuscitation, calcitonin, bisphosphonates
hypercalcemia.core: Elevated calcium causes stones, constipation, polyuria, weakness, and neuropsychiatric changes; PTH distinguishes hormone-driven disease from other causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Parathyroid adenoma/hyperplasia, malignancy, prolonged immobilization
Thiazides, lithium, excess vitamin D or calcium/absorbable alkali, granulomatous disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Dehydration, nausea, abdominal pain, reduced reflexes; ECG may show shortened QT
★ **Calcium >14 mg/dL**, confusion, arrhythmia, or severe volume depletion → urgent treatment
Primary hyperparathyroidism often asymptomatic; malignancy-associated disease tends to progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PTH promotes bone resorption and renal calcium retention while increasing phosphate excretion
Hypercalcemia impairs renal concentration → dehydration, reduced calcium clearance, self-reinforcing elevation
High filtered calcium exceeds tubular reabsorption → **hypercalciuria** → calcium stones

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm with repeat total/albumin-adjusted or **ionized calcium**, especially with altered proteins or critical illness
★ **Intact PTH first**; elevated or inappropriately normal → PTH-dependent
Suppressed PTH → PTHrP, vitamin D metabolites, malignancy/myeloma evaluation guided by context
Primary disease versus FHH → urine calcium; clearance ratio <0.01 favors FHH, with overlap
Parathyroid imaging localizes before surgery; never establishes biochemical diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe/symptomatic → **IV isotonic saline**, then calcitonin for rapid temporary lowering
★ **Denosumab** (favored, esp renal limitation/refractory) or **IV zoledronic acid/pamidronate** for sustained malignancy control
Calcitriol-mediated disease → glucocorticoids; dialysis for refractory life-threatening elevation or inability to hydrate
Primary disease: surgery for symptoms, age <50, calcium >1 above ULN, osteoporosis/fracture, stones, eGFR <60
Stop causative supplements/drugs; loop diuretic only for fluid overload, not routine calcium elimination

rows.label: Complications
items: Nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, AKI, osteoporosis/fractures, pancreatitis
Calcitonin tachyphylaxis after 48–72 hours; antiresorptives can cause hypocalcemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration, avoid excess calcium/alkali; monitor calcium, renal function, and bone density when observing primary disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: FHH: lifelong mild elevation, family history, hypocalciuria; surgery ineffective
Pseudohypercalcemia: high protein-bound calcium but normal ionized fraction

hypercalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established calcium evaluation and emergency management.

hyponatremia.name: Hyponatremia
hyponatremia.scope: Hypovolemic, euvolemic (SIADH, primary polydipsia), hypervolemic, acute vs chronic, hypertonic saline indications
hyponatremia.core: Low serum sodium reflects excess water relative to sodium; symptoms and duration determine urgency before the cause determines maintenance treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine, oxytocin; **hypotonic IV D5W**, postoperative state, exercise + excess water
Pulmonary/CNS disease; **small cell lung cancer** (ectopic ADH); heart failure, cirrhosis, renal failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, headache, gait instability; seizures, coma or marked confusion indicate severe cerebral edema
Orthostasis/dry mucosa suggest depletion; edema/ascites suggest excess extracellular fluid
SIADH: clinically euvolemic with inappropriately concentrated urine despite hypo-osmolality
Massive water intake, often psychiatric illness; urine osmolality below serum still favors polydipsia, even if >100

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hypotonic extracellular fluid drives water into brain; chronic adaptation makes rapid correction dangerous
ADH-mediated water retention or intake exceeding renal dilution capacity lowers sodium concentration
Low effective volume (heart failure, cirrhosis, diarrhea) → baroreceptor ADH release; total-body sodium high in edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Serum osmolality first: **<275 mOsm/kg** confirms hypotonicity; assess glucose and volume status
Hyperglycemia → translocational hyponatremia; severe hyperlipidemia/proteinemia → pseudohyponatremia
★ Urine osmolality **<100** → polydipsia/low solute; ≥100 → persistent ADH activity
Urine Na <20–30 suggests low effective arterial volume; >30 suggests renal loss or SIADH
Exclude adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism and renal failure before diagnosing SIADH; diuretics confound urine Na

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe neurologic symptoms → **3% saline bolus**, repeated for initial Na rise 4–6 mEq/L
Hypovolemia → isotonic saline; SIADH → fluid restriction, increased solute, remove trigger
Edematous states → fluid/sodium restriction and loop diuretic; treat heart/liver/kidney disorder
★ Chronic/unknown duration: generally limit rise to **≤8 mEq/L per 24 h**; monitor frequently
Overcorrection → desmopressin plus D5W; avoid routine vaptans in acute symptomatic cases

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute severe hyponatremia → herniation, respiratory arrest
Osmotic demyelination after rapid correction; greatest risk with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid hypotonic maintenance fluids during high ADH states; review causative drugs
Monitor for brisk aquaresis after restoring volume or stopping thiazides

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cerebral salt wasting: neurosurgical patient, hypovolemic, high urine Na; SIADH euvolemic
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemia: measured osmolality elevated
Primary psychiatric disease: neurologic change without sodium abnormality

hyponatremia.evidence: Not checked online; established hyponatremia consensus principles.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.scope: Hashimoto thyroiditis, subclinical hypothyroidism, myxedema coma, autoimmune associations, levothyroxine dosing, TSH monitoring
hypothyroidism.core: Insufficient thyroid hormone slows metabolism, causing fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, and delayed reflex relaxation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hashimoto autoimmunity, family history of autoimmune disease; thyroid surgery/radioiodine, iodine deficiency/excess
Lithium, amiodarone, postpartum thyroiditis; pituitary surgery/radiation or mass
Congenital primary → **thyroid dysgenesis** most common, not lymphocytic thyroiditis

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight gain, bradycardia, hoarseness, heavy menses, hyperlipidemia; hyponatremia in severe disease
★ **Hypothermia, altered mentation, hypoventilation, hypotension** → myxedema coma
Autoimmune clustering: type 1 diabetes, pernicious anemia, adrenal insufficiency, celiac disease
Infant: macroglossia, umbilical hernia, prolonged jaundice, hypotonia, large fontanelle → **TSH/free T4**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced hormone activity lowers thermogenesis and cardiac output; glycosaminoglycan deposition produces nonpitting edema
Hashimoto: lymphocytic infiltration; firm painless goiter, even if euthyroid; **anti-TPO/antithyroglobulin** antibodies

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH and free T4** establish hormone deficiency and localize the level of dysfunction
Positive anti-TPO predicts progression from subclinical disease; ultrasound unnecessary without nodule/goiter concern
Recheck mild isolated TSH elevation after transient illness resolves; exclude medication interference

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Levothyroxine**; healthy young adult approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day; older/CAD start 12.5–25 mcg/day
Fasting, apart from calcium/iron; TSH at 6–8 weeks; **persistently high → increase dose**, even if asymptomatic
Central disease: titrate using free T4; evaluate/replace cortisol before thyroid hormone
Subclinical, untreated: generally start at TSH ≥10; consider symptoms, antibodies, pregnancy at lower values
★ Myxedema: **IV levothyroxine + IV hydrocortisone**, airway support, cautious fluids/passive warming; treat trigger

rows.label: Complications
items: Dyslipidemia, infertility, pericardial effusion, neuropathy; severe disease → respiratory failure
Excess replacement → AF, angina, bone loss; rapid correction in CAD can precipitate ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Pregnancy: early **TSH monitoring**, usually increase existing replacement promptly; use pregnancy-specific targets
Monitor stable replacement at least annually; address adherence/absorption before escalating doses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Depression, dementia, psychosis: normal TSH; hypothyroidism itself can cause reversible cognitive or psychiatric symptoms
Euthyroid sick syndrome: acute systemic illness, often low T3; avoid routine hormone replacement

hypothyroidism.evidence: Not checked online; established thyroid replacement and endocrine emergency teaching.

infectious-mononucleosis.name: Infectious mononucleosis
infectious-mononucleosis.scope: Epstein-Barr virus, triad of fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, atypical lymphocytes, heterophile antibody test, splenic rupture precautions
infectious-mononucleosis.core: An adolescent or young adult with fever, exudative pharyngitis, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and prolonged fatigue likely has EBV mononucleosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Salivary transmission, close intimate contact, shared drink containers; primary symptomatic infection often in adolescence
Immunocompromised patients face greater risk of EBV-related lymphoproliferative disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Palatal petechiae, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, mild hepatomegaly/transaminase elevation
★ **Atypical lymphocytes** on smear; reactive cells are CD8 T lymphocytes, not infected B cells
★ Diffuse rash after **amoxicillin/ampicillin** supports EBV; not automatically lifelong penicillin allergy
Severe tonsillar enlargement with stridor/drooling → assess airway immediately

rows.label: Pathophys
items: EBV infects B cells via CD21; cytotoxic immune response produces systemic symptoms and lymphocytosis
Reticuloendothelial expansion enlarges spleen and weakens its capsule

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Heterophile antibody test** with CBC in typical presentation
False negatives early in illness and in young children → EBV-specific serology
Acute infection: VCA IgM positive with absent EBNA; EBNA develops later and persists
Mononucleosis-like illness with negative EBV tests → consider CMV and acute HIV testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Hydration, rest, acetaminophen/NSAID, viscous lidocaine gargle**; gradual activity as symptoms improve
No routine antibiotics, antivirals, or glucocorticoids for uncomplicated disease
Steroids only for threatened airway or severe immune complications, such as hemolysis/thrombocytopenia
Sudden LUQ pain, referred left shoulder pain, syncope → urgent splenic rupture evaluation and resuscitation

rows.label: Complications
items: Splenic rupture, airway obstruction, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia
Hepatitis, prolonged fatigue; rare neurologic involvement; avoid alcohol during significant liver inflammation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **No athletic activity for first 3 weeks** from onset; then light noncontact activity if recovered
Contact/collision sports and heavy lifting deferred until recovery and individualized clearance; usually ≥3–4 weeks
No routine ultrasound solely to clear athletes; avoid sharing saliva-contaminated objects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Streptococcal pharyngitis: anterior nodes, no typical atypical lymphocytosis or splenic enlargement
CMV: heterophile-negative syndrome, less prominent pharyngitis
Acute HIV: exposure history, rash/mucosal ulcers; antigen/antibody plus RNA testing

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers
Leading cause of cancer death in men and women; smoking is the predominant risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action
Painful long-bone periostitis ± clubbing/joint swelling → **hypertrophic osteoarthropathy**, a lung cancer complication

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes
Central endobronchial tumor → bronchial obstruction → **post-obstructive pneumonia**, atelectasis, lobar collapse
Ectopic **ACTH** (polypeptide; cortisol excess secondary) → hyperpigmentation, hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis, proximal weakness

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used
SVC syndrome from small-cell → urgent **chemotherapy** ± radiation; stent if severe; diuretics not definitive

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production
Preterm birth → low stores, screen toddlers; infant microcytosis → **dietary history** for excess cow's milk

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV, preserved hemoglobin, high RBC count, **normal RDW** (Mentzer <13) suggest thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release; cytokines blunt **erythropoietin**
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead
Microcytosis + afebrile pain crisis, at-risk ancestry → **smear** for sickled cells (sickle–β-thalassemia)

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool
Four-gene α-deletion → **Hb Barts** (γ4) → severe fetal anemia, hydrops fetalis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

myeloproliferative-neoplasms.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasms
myeloproliferative-neoplasms.scope: CML, polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, primary myelofibrosis
myeloproliferative-neoplasms.core: Clonal marrow proliferation elevates mature blood-cell counts or causes progressive fibrosis; thrombosis and transformation drive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually acquired stem-cell mutations in adults; age and prior thrombosis predict vascular risk
Prior radiation exposure associated with CML; no common lifestyle trigger explains most cases

rows.label: Clues
items: Splenomegaly, fatigue, early satiety, constitutional symptoms; markedly abnormal CBC may be incidental
★ **Aquagenic pruritus**, erythromelalgia or unexplained splanchnic thrombosis → evaluate clonal disease
Very high platelets may paradoxically cause mucosal bleeding through acquired von Willebrand dysfunction
PV with headache, visual/CNS hyperviscosity symptoms → **urgent phlebotomy** before relying on aspirin

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Constitutive tyrosine-kinase signaling produces growth independent of normal feedback
Myelofibrosis → cytokine-driven fibrosis and extramedullary hematopoiesis; not simply excess fibroblast clonality

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear**, erythropoietin with erythrocytosis; marrow biopsy and mutation testing classify disease
PV thresholds: hemoglobin >16.5 g/dL men/>16 women or hematocrit >49%/>48%, with diagnostic context
ET requires persistent platelets ≥450,000/µL plus marrow/molecular findings and exclusion of reactive causes
Teardrops and leukoerythroblastosis support fibrosis; marrow aspiration may yield dry tap

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ PV → **phlebotomy to hematocrit <45%** plus low-dose aspirin if safe
PV/ET high thrombotic risk → hydroxyurea; interferon favored for selected younger/pregnant patients
★ CML → **BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor**, e.g., imatinib; monitor molecular response
Symptomatic myelofibrosis → JAK inhibitor such as ruxolitinib; allogeneic transplant potentially curative
Extreme thrombocytosis with bleeding → assess von Willebrand function before aspirin; urgent cytoreduction if critical

rows.label: Complications
items: Arterial/venous thrombosis, hemorrhage, hyperuricemia; secondary myelofibrosis or AML
CML blast phase: ≥20% blasts; advanced disease needs acute-leukemia-directed specialist treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Cardiovascular risk control; disease-specific count control, pregnancy planning, monitor progression

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive thrombocytosis: iron deficiency/inflammation; secondary erythrocytosis: hypoxia or ↑EPO
Leukemoid reaction: toxic granulation, infection trigger, absent BCR-ABL

myeloproliferative-neoplasms.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

nutritional-deficiencies.name: Nutritional deficiencies
nutritional-deficiencies.scope: Vegan diet nutrient risks, tea-and-toast diet, vitamin and mineral supplementation, clinical manifestations
nutritional-deficiencies.core: Restricted intake, malabsorption, or increased requirements produce characteristic mucocutaneous, neurologic, hematologic, and skeletal findings; identify the missing nutrient and its cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unsupplemented vegan diet: B12, iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, zinc risks
Tea-and-toast diet, alcohol misuse, food insecurity, restrictive eating, institutionalization
Bariatric surgery, pancreatic insufficiency, cholestasis, bowel disease → specific or fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor wound healing, bruising, oral changes, neuropathy, bone pain; mixed deficiencies commonly coexist
★ **Confusion, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia** in malnutrition → thiamine deficiency; complete triad often absent
Night blindness → vitamin A; bleeding with prolonged PT → vitamin K
Dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia → niacin; periorificial/acral dermatitis, alopecia, dysgeusia → zinc (TPN, penicillamine)

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insufficient cofactors impair energy metabolism, collagen formation, hematopoiesis, or mineralization
Low intake differs from malabsorption: replacement route and lasting supplementation must match the mechanism
Vitamin D deficiency → ↓calcium absorption → **secondary hyperparathyroidism**: normal calcium at bone's expense

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diet and supplement history**, weight trend, oral/skin/neurologic examination; assess GI disease
CBC/ferritin, B12 ± methylmalonic acid, 25-OH vitamin D chosen by findings; avoid indiscriminate panels
Albumin is altered by inflammation/fluid status; not a stand-alone nutrition diagnostic test
Severely undernourished → baseline phosphate, Mg, K before nutritional rehabilitation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected Wernicke syndrome → **parenteral thiamine promptly**; do not await laboratory confirmation
B12 deficiency with neurologic signs/malabsorption → parenteral replacement; folate only after B12 assessment
Vitamin D/calcium for deficient intake or osteomalacia; iron replacement with evaluation for blood loss
Vitamin C for scurvy; oral balanced nutrition plus cause-directed supplementation and dietitian support
★ Severe malnutrition → **slow refeeding + thiamine**, close phosphate/K/Mg monitoring and replacement

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible B12 neurologic injury, fractures, anemia, infection susceptibility
Refeeding → hypophosphatemia, arrhythmia, respiratory failure; excess vitamin A → hepatotoxicity/teratogenicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Vegans → **reliable B12 supplementation**; fortified foods, calcium/vitamin D and iodine adequacy
Diversified diet, food access support, lifelong bariatric follow-up; avoid megadose supplementation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Scurvy versus vasculitis: perifollicular hemorrhage/corkscrew hairs, swollen bleeding gums, restricted produce intake
Hypothyroidism: fatigue and macrocytosis with elevated TSH

nutritional-deficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established nutritional deficiency and refeeding principles.

organophosphate-poisoning.name: Organophosphate poisoning
organophosphate-poisoning.scope: Organophosphates, carbamates, muscarinic and nicotinic toxidrome, atropine, pralidoxime
organophosphate-poisoning.core: A wet cholinergic toxidrome with bronchorrhea, miosis and weakness after pesticide exposure requires atropine, respiratory support and early pralidoxime.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Agricultural insecticides, contaminated clothing, intentional ingestion or nerve-agent exposure
Carbamates produce a similar but usually shorter-lived cholinergic syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Muscarinic: salivation, lacrimation, diarrhea, urination, emesis, sweating, bronchospasm and bradycardia
Nicotinic: **fasciculations followed by weakness/paralysis**; tachycardia/hypertension may coexist
CNS: confusion, seizures, coma; pinpoint pupils may be absent with mixed exposures
★ Copious airway secretions and respiratory muscle weakness → impending ventilatory failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Acetylcholinesterase inhibition increases synaptic acetylcholine at muscarinic, nicotinic and CNS receptors
Organophosphate enzyme binding becomes irreversible after aging; carbamate inhibition is generally reversible

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical toxidrome** determines treatment; do not await cholinesterase results
RBC acetylcholinesterase and plasma butyrylcholinesterase support exposure; baseline values often unavailable
ABG, glucose, electrolytes, ECG; assess aspiration and oxygenation after airway stabilization
Pulse oximetry does not exclude hypercapnia from respiratory muscle failure

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Skin-absorbed → staff **chemical-resistant gloves**, not just mask/goggles; remove clothes, **wash skin**, irrigate eyes
Suction, oxygen and early intubation for weak ventilation; avoid succinylcholine because paralysis may be prolonged
★ Repeated escalating **atropine** until pulmonary secretions/bronchospasm improve; pupil size is not the endpoint
★ **Pralidoxime early**, before aging, restores enzyme and treats nicotinic weakness; atropine remains essential
Seizures/agitation → benzodiazepine; activated charcoal only for selected early ingestion with protected airway

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory arrest, aspiration pneumonia, dysrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
Intermediate syndrome: delayed proximal/respiratory weakness after initial recovery; delayed peripheral neuropathy possible
Excess atropine → antimuscarinic delirium/hyperthermia; titrate to pulmonary findings

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safe pesticide storage, protective equipment, occupational education and exposure surveillance
Observe after improvement for recurrent toxicity; evaluate intent and psychosocial risk after deliberate ingestion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Opioids: miosis/respiratory depression without profuse secretions or fasciculations
Antimuscarinic poisoning: dry skin, mydriasis, urinary retention
Carbamate exposure: oximes usually unnecessary when isolated exposure confirmed

osteonecrosis.name: Osteonecrosis
osteonecrosis.scope: Avascular necrosis of femoral head, risk factors (corticosteroids, alcohol, sickle cell, trauma), MRI sensitivity, crescent sign on plain radiograph, core decompression, joint replacement
osteonecrosis.core: Progressive deep hip or groin pain after steroid exposure, heavy alcohol use, sickle cell disease, or trauma suggests femoral-head ischemia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Glucocorticoids**, excessive alcohol, sickle cell vaso-occlusion, femoral neck fracture or hip dislocation
SLE, transplantation, decompression exposure; bilateral disease common with systemic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight-bearing pain progressing to rest/night pain; limited internal rotation and abduction
Antalgic gait, referred thigh/knee pain; early examination can be nearly normal
Sudden worsening suggests subchondral fracture or articular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Interrupted subchondral blood supply → osteocyte death, microfractures, eventual joint surface collapse
Repair cannot keep pace with mechanical loading; secondary degenerative arthritis follows

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AP pelvis and lateral hip radiographs** first; early disease may be radiographically occult
★ Persistent suspicion despite normal films → **MRI**, most sensitive early test
Later films: patchy sclerosis/lucency; crescent sign indicates subchondral fracture, then flattening
Evaluate contralateral hip when symptoms or systemic risk suggest bilateral involvement

rows.label: Tx
items: Protected weight-bearing, cane/crutches, NSAIDs, orthopedic referral; analgesics do not restore perfusion
★ Before collapse → **core decompression** in selected symptomatic lesions; joint-preserving options depend on extent
Advanced collapse or secondary arthritis → total hip arthroplasty
Reduce avoidable steroid/alcohol exposure; manage sickle cell and other underlying disorders

rows.label: Complications
items: Femoral-head collapse, painful osteoarthritis, loss of mobility and function
Arthroplasty: infection, dislocation, loosening; younger patients may require revision

rows.label: Prevention
items: Use lowest effective glucocorticoid exposure; counsel against heavy alcohol consumption
Prompt reduction of traumatic hip dislocation limits ischemic time; monitor high-risk post-traumatic hips
Activity modification during evaluation reduces loading on vulnerable subchondral bone

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hip osteoarthritis: gradual activity pain, joint-space narrowing and osteophytes rather than early isolated necrosis
Septic arthritis: fever, severe pain with passive motion; urgent aspiration
Femoral neck stress fracture: overuse, fracture line or marrow edema on MRI
Osteomyelitis: fever, elevated ESR/CRP; osteonecrosis markers usually normal

osteonecrosis.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic diagnosis and stage-based treatment.

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
pancreatitis.core: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with pancreatic inflammation may be acute; repeated injury produces irreversible chronic insufficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gallstones (prior postprandial biliary colic), heavy alcohol, triglycerides >1,000 mg/dL, ERCP, hypercalcemia, medications
Chronic: prolonged alcohol/tobacco exposure, genetic disease, duct obstruction, autoimmune disease
Blunt abdominal trauma + epigastric mass/raised enzymes → contrast CT for pancreatic/duodenal injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue: ↓insulin, ↓glucagon, normal insulin sensitivity; lipase may normalize

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase or amylase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT: diagnostic doubt, high fever/marked leukocytosis (necrosis?), deterioration, no improvement by 48–72 hours; not routine early
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency
Recurrent, no gallstones/alcohol → EUS or MRCP for ductal anatomy; older exam questions may expect ERCP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, reassessment, IV opioid analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** by 48 hours if tolerated; else enteral; older exam questions may expect initial bowel rest
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Uncomplicated/sterile: no antibiotics; infected necrosis: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancrelipase, fat-soluble vitamins, pain control; islet-loss diabetes → **insulin**, not sulfonylureas

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; necrosis, hemorrhage; **splenic vein thrombosis** → isolated gastric varices, normal liver
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
rows: Transient dysfunction ≤48 hours or local complication

perioperative-care.name: Perioperative care
perioperative-care.scope: Preoperative cardiac risk, pulmonary evaluation, surgical antibiotic prophylaxis, medication management, pain control
perioperative-care.core: Optimize active disease, estimate procedural and patient risk, and order testing only when the result could change perioperative management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **MI within 60 days**, decompensated HF → highest perioperative cardiac risk; older exam questions may expect MI within 6 months
Emergency, vascular or intrathoracic surgery; ischemic heart disease, heart failure, CKD, diabetes
Smoking, COPD, OSA, frailty, malnutrition and prior anesthesia complications

rows.label: Clues
items: Chest pain, new dyspnea, syncope or decompensated fluid overload require targeted evaluation
Poor functional capacity: inability to climb stairs or perform activities around 4 METs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Surgical stress raises myocardial oxygen demand; anesthesia can lower perfusion pressure
Sedation, pain and recumbency reduce ventilation and promote atelectasis and venous stasis
Surgical stress, pain, opioids → nonosmotic **ADH** release → transient oliguria with normal renal function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RCRI/NSQIP** plus functional assessment; no routine stress test for low-risk surgery
Elevated risk, poor/unknown capacity → stress test if management changes; cannot exercise → **pharmacologic stress imaging**
ECG for cardiovascular symptoms; echo for new/worsening HF or suspected significant valve disease
No routine chest radiograph/spirometry without respiratory findings; assess airway and OSA history
Lung resection: **predicted postoperative FEV1** best predictor of complications; predicted postoperative FEV1 <30–40% → high risk, exercise testing before deciding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Active ACS, decompensated HF or unstable arrhythmia → defer elective surgery and stabilize
★ Continue chronic **beta blockers/statins**; do not start beta blockade on surgery day
Hold **SGLT2 inhibitors 3–4 days**; individualize GLP-1 drugs by aspiration risk; continue reduced basal insulin
★ **Cefazolin within 60 minutes** before incision; MRSA or severe beta-lactam allergy → vancomycin within 120 minutes
Multimodal analgesia: acetaminophen, regional block, selective NSAID; add opioid by severity, respiratory monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Myocardial injury, AKI, delirium, pneumonia, VTE and surgical-site infection
Opioids aggravate OSA; excessive fluids can worsen pulmonary edema
New postoperative dyspnea, ↓basal breath sounds → chest radiograph first, before PE imaging or heparin

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, lung expansion exercises, early mobilization, mechanical/pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis
Anticoagulation interruption individualized; bridging reserved for highest thrombotic risk
Chronic steroid exposure with adrenal suppression → perioperative glucocorticoid coverage
Usable gut → **enteral feeding**, including distal jejunostomy, over TPN

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anxiety-related dyspnea: normal cardiopulmonary evaluation
Stable chronic disease: baseline symptoms alone do not mandate cancellation

table.title: Postoperative pain
rows: Severe pain after major abdominal surgery

pilonidal-disease.name: Pilonidal disease
pilonidal-disease.scope: Pilonidal cyst, acute pilonidal abscess, sinus tract with pits, incision and drainage, wound care, recurrence
pilonidal-disease.core: Acquired hair-driven inflammation in the natal cleft ranges from incidental pits to painful abscesses and chronically draining sinuses.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young adults, male sex, dense body hair, deep gluteal cleft, obesity
Prolonged sitting, friction, sweating; family predisposition and prior episodes increase recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Midline pits over the sacrococcygeal cleft**, sometimes containing hair/debris
Acute tender erythematous fluctuant swelling; drainage can arise through lateral openings
Recurrent serous/purulent discharge with induration suggests persistent sinus; systemic toxicity unusual in localized disease
Lesions close to anal verge or atypical openings → evaluate another diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loose hairs penetrate cleft skin → foreign-body reaction and secondary infection
Persistent cavities/tracts permit repeated inflammation rather than representing a congenital spinal connection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical examination** of cleft and perianal region; imaging usually unnecessary
Assess fever, surrounding cellulitis, immunocompromise and extent of fluctuance
Atypical deep/recurrent disease near anus → MRI or colorectal evaluation for fistula/Crohn disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute abscess → **incision and drainage**; do not substitute oral antibiotics
Cellulitis → cephalexin ± TMP-SMX for MRSA risk; systemic toxicity/immunocompromise → hospital assessment
After drainage → analgesia, dressing changes and cleansing; reassess wound healing
★ Persistent/recurrent symptomatic sinus → elective **excision or minimally invasive tract procedure**
Complex disease → off-midline flap/closure preferred over primary midline closure; asymptomatic pits generally observed

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent abscess, persistent sinus and drainage, delayed wound healing; extensive surgery may cause prolonged recovery
Repeated inflammation → scarring, impaired sitting/activity; postoperative wound dehiscence or infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cleft hygiene, reduce retained hair/friction; consider laser hair removal, especially recurrent disease
Smoking cessation and weight management support healing; recurrence remains possible after any procedure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epidermoid cyst: punctum away from characteristic cleft pits
Furuncle: isolated infected follicle without persistent sinus system

table.title: Other anogenital sinus disorders
rows: External opening connects toward anal canal

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural effusion
pleural-effusion.scope: Transudate vs exudate (Light criteria), parapneumonic effusion, empyema, malignant effusion
pleural-effusion.core: Fluid in the pleural space causes dyspnea, dullness, and reduced breath sounds; classify by mechanism and identify infection requiring drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome; pneumonia, malignancy, pulmonary embolism, TB
Recent thoracic surgery, pancreatitis, esophageal rupture, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pleuritic pain, reduced fremitus; large effusion shifts mediastinum away; unilateral + cancer history → malignant
Fever or persistent sepsis despite antibiotics suggests complicated parapneumonic fluid/empyema
Bloody fluid: malignancy (prior cancer, mediastinal mass), embolism, trauma; milky → chyle
Foul-smelling pus after aspiration → **anaerobic empyema**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transudate: altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure; exudate: increased permeability or impaired lymphatic drainage
Heart-failure transudate: pleural protein <3 g/dL, low LDH and cell count; **glucose equals serum**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Chest radiograph → **ultrasound-guided thoracentesis** for new unexplained, unilateral, or atypical effusion
Classic bilateral heart-failure effusions → diuresis first; sample if fever, asymmetry, or treatment failure
★ **Exudate if any Light criterion** positive; compare paired pleural and serum measurements
Pleural pH, glucose, cell differential, Gram stain/culture; cytology if cancer suspected
Diuresis can create pseudoexudate; serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL supports transudate

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat systemic cause; therapeutic thoracentesis for significant symptoms; avoid rapid excessive drainage
★ Pus, positive Gram stain/culture, **pH <7.20** or glucose <60 → empyema/complicated: chest tube, antibiotics
Loculated infected fluid → intrapleural tPA/DNase; persistent sepsis → VATS evaluation
★ Recurrent symptomatic malignancy → **indwelling pleural catheter** or pleurodesis; trapped lung favors catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, loculation, trapped lung, respiratory compromise
Thoracentesis → pneumothorax, bleeding, reexpansion pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Heart-failure control, prompt pneumonia treatment; ultrasound guidance reduces procedural injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atelectasis: mediastinal shift toward volume loss
Consolidation: increased fremitus, bronchial breath sounds
Pneumothorax: hyperresonance rather than dullness

pleural-effusion.evidence: Not checked online; established pleural disease teaching.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.scope: Community-acquired, hospital-acquired, ventilator-associated, aspiration, atypical pneumonia (Legionella, Mycoplasma)
pneumonia.core: Acute lower respiratory infection with a new infiltrate; severity, acquisition setting, and resistance risks determine disposition and empiric antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, COPD, age, immunosuppression
Dysphagia, absent gag/cough (stroke, dementia, Parkinson), impaired consciousness → aspiration
HAP ≥48 hours hospitalized; VAP ≥48 hours after intubation
Prior MRSA/Pseudomonas isolation or recent hospitalization with IV antibiotics → resistant pathogens

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, cough, sputum, focal crackles; older adults: confusion; children: lower-lobe disease may refer abdominal pain
★ Severe: **hypoxemia, hypotension, tachypnea**, multilobar disease; ventilation or pressors → ICU
Legionella: water exposure, diarrhea, hyponatremia; Mycoplasma: school-age/young adult, indolent dry cough, cold agglutinins
Immunocompromised, diffuse bilateral interstitial/alveolar infiltrates, exertional hypoxemia → **Pneumocystis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar inflammation/exudate → shunt and impaired oxygenation
Chemical aspiration pneumonitis: sterile gastric injury; severity tracks **volume and acidity**; rapid improvement possible

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CXR** first; CT if strong suspicion despite nondiagnostic radiograph
**CURB-65** 0–1 or low PSI → outpatient; severe CAP → blood/sputum cultures, Legionella antigen ± PCR
Low procalcitonin alone does not justify withholding initial antibiotics in radiographically confirmed bacterial CAP
Gram-positive lancet diplococci → **S pneumoniae**: commonest CAP; lobar consolidation, high fever, often post-viral URI
Small gram-negative coccobacilli, smoker/COPD → **H influenzae**

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen, fluids for hypoperfusion; drain empyema; narrow antibiotics to cultures
★ Aspiration pneumonia: usual CAP coverage; **add anaerobic coverage only for abscess/empyema**
Anaerobes: **ampicillin-sulbactam**; older exam questions may expect **clindamycin**, even without abscess
Stable nonsevere CAP: ATS 2025 permits 3–4 days; classic ≥5-day rule remains for severe disease
★ Severe noninfluenza CAP → consider **systemic corticosteroids**; nonsevere CAP → avoid routine steroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Parapneumonic effusion, empyema, bacteremia, respiratory failure, sepsis
S aureus: postinfluenza necrotizing pneumonia; child failing amoxicillin, dense consolidation/effusion
Aspiration (alcoholism, intubation) → **lung abscess**: dependent-segment cavity, air-fluid level, foul sputum
Antibiotic exposure → C difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, smoking cessation, swallowing evaluation
Aspiration/VAP prevention: head elevation 30–45°, oral care, early liberation from ventilation

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: thrombotic risk, pleuritic pain, no infectious source
HF: bilateral edema, elevated JVP, cardiac dysfunction

table.title: Empiric adult regimens
rows: Amoxicillin/clavulanate + azithromycin; doxycycline alternative; or levofloxacin
Antipseudomonal: cefepime, ceftazidime, or piperacillin/tazobactam; usually 7 days

polycystic-kidney-disease.name: Polycystic kidney disease
polycystic-kidney-disease.scope: Autosomal dominant PKD, 50% inheritance risk, hypertension control, berry aneurysms, hepatic cysts, MVP, tolvaptan
polycystic-kidney-disease.core: Autosomal dominant cystic kidney disease produces progressive bilateral renal enlargement and systemic manifestations; family history guides diagnosis and targeted screening.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heterozygous PKD1 or PKD2 variants; each child has 50% transmission risk
PKD1 generally progresses earlier; hypertension, large kidney volume and early renal decline predict worse course

rows.label: Clues
items: Flank discomfort, palpable kidneys, recurrent hematuria, stones, UTIs or early hypertension
★ Fever and persistent focal pain → **cyst infection**, even with nondiagnostic urine culture
Sudden severe headache/meningeal signs → possible aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage; emergency evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal polycystin signaling promotes tubular cyst expansion and interstitial fibrosis
Intrarenal ischemia activates RAAS; cyst burden progressively reduces functional nephron mass

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Renal ultrasound** first with family history; MRI/CT if equivocal or for kidney-volume assessment
Monitor BP, creatinine/eGFR, urine albumin; genetic testing when uncertain diagnosis or reproductive/donor decisions
★ Aneurysm screening with **noncontrast MRA** for personal SAH or family aneurysm/SAH/unexplained sudden death
Do not routinely screen every patient for intracranial aneurysm; discuss additional individualized risk contexts

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **ACE inhibitor or ARB** for hypertension, especially albuminuria; avoid during pregnancy
Rapidly progressive adult disease with eGFR ≥25 → consider **tolvaptan**; monitor liver tests, polyuria and dehydration
Cyst infection → cyst-penetrating antibiotic such as ciprofloxacin based on cultures; drain refractory large infected cyst
Hematuria → rest, hydration and exclude stone/tumor if persistent; severe bleeding → embolization
Advanced kidney failure → dialysis/transplant evaluation; avoid chronic NSAIDs

rows.label: Complications
items: **CKD → ESKD** most common long-term complication; hepatic cysts, intracranial aneurysms, MVP, diverticulosis, infection
Tolvaptan → hepatotoxicity and aquaresis; aneurysm rupture → catastrophic hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Genetic/reproductive counseling; smoking cessation, sodium reduction, BP control; avoid dehydration on aquaretic treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Simple cysts: few incidental lesions without enlarged kidneys/familial pattern
ARPKD: neonate, bilateral enlarged echogenic kidneys, congenital hepatic fibrosis
Acquired cystic disease: longstanding CKD/dialysis
Wilms tumor/neuroblastoma: solid, usually unilateral mass, not bilateral cystic nephromegaly

polyuria-diabetes-insipidus.name: Polyuria and diabetes insipidus
polyuria-diabetes-insipidus.scope: Central diabetes insipidus, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (lithium, hypercalcemia), water deprivation test, desmopressin response
polyuria-diabetes-insipidus.core: Large-volume dilute urine requires separation of water diuresis from solute diuresis; impaired thirst or water access makes diabetes insipidus dangerous.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central: sellar surgery/trauma/infiltration; nephrogenic: lithium, hypercalcemia, hypokalemia or inherited defects
Primary polydipsia: excessive voluntary intake, psychiatric disease; osmotic diuresis: diabetes mellitus, mannitol

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria >3 L/day in adults, nocturia, polydipsia; distinguish from frequent small-volume voiding
★ **Hypernatremia with urine osmolality <300 mOsm/kg** suggests inadequate antidiuretic effect
Low/low-normal sodium favors excess drinking; dehydration, weakness or altered mentation signals severe water deficit

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insufficient vasopressin signaling prevents collecting-duct aquaporin-mediated water reabsorption
Lithium enters collecting-duct cells through ENaC and impairs concentrating ability

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **24-hour urine volume**; serum Na/osmolality, urine osmolality, glucose, calcium, K, creatinine
Hyperglycemia with concentrated solute-rich urine → osmotic diuresis; no need for water deprivation
★ Stable hypotonic polyuria → **supervised water deprivation followed by desmopressin**, or stimulated copeptin testing
Avoid dehydration testing in existing hypernatremia/volume depletion; partial defects may yield overlapping responses
Established central disease → pituitary MRI and anterior-axis evaluation; check lithium level with exposure

rows.label: Tx
items: Shock → isotonic resuscitation first; then oral/IV free water with serial sodium monitoring
★ Central → **desmopressin**; avoid excess water intake and monitor for hyponatremia
Nephrogenic → remove cause, low-solute diet, thiazide; lithium-associated → amiloride
Lithium toxicity → stop drug, isotonic fluids; severe neurologic effects/impaired clearance → hemodialysis consultation
Primary polydipsia → address cause and supervised intake plan; desmopressin risks water intoxication

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypernatremic encephalopathy, seizures, hypovolemic shock; overly rapid chronic sodium correction → cerebral edema
Desmopressin/excess drinking → hyponatremic seizures; chronic lithium → CKD

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Reliable water access, sick-day plan; lithium renal/electrolyte monitoring and avoidance of volume depletion
Mild lithium DI, intact thirst, normal sodium → **keep drinking**; fluid restriction risks hypernatremic dehydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: Overactive bladder/UTI: frequency without increased total volume
Postobstructive diuresis: follows relief of retention; monitor fluid/electrolyte losses

polyuria-diabetes-insipidus.evidence: Testing update checked 2026-10-30: [Endotext AVP deficiency/resistance, 2026](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279011/); classic testing patterns: established teaching.

rheumatoid-arthritis.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
rheumatoid-arthritis.scope: Symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis, anti-CCP and RF, DMARDs (methotrexate, biologics), extra-articular manifestations, Felty syndrome, cervical spine subluxation
rheumatoid-arthritis.core: Persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis with prolonged morning stiffness and improvement with activity; early disease-modifying treatment prevents erosions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Female sex, smoking, family history, HLA-DRB1 susceptibility; onset often middle adulthood

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Boggy swelling of **MCP, PIP, wrists**; DIP joints usually spared
Ulnar deviation, swan-neck/boutonnière deformities; subcutaneous nodules and constitutional symptoms
Extra-articular: pleuritis, interstitial lung disease, episcleritis/scleritis, pericarditis, neuropathy
★ **Felty syndrome**: established erosive disease + splenomegaly + neutropenia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Autoimmune synovial inflammation → pannus, cartilage destruction, marginal bone erosion
TNF and other inflammatory cytokines drive articular and systemic injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical synovitis → **anti-CCP, RF, ESR/CRP**; anti-CCP more specific, negative serology not exclusionary
Hand/foot radiographs: periarticular osteopenia, uniform narrowing, erosions; early films can be normal
Acute single hot joint → arthrocentesis to exclude infection or crystals before attributing symptoms
Neck pain, neurologic symptoms, or suspected instability before anesthesia → cervical imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Methotrexate + folate** first-line for moderate/high activity; hydroxychloroquine reasonable for low activity
Treat to remission/low activity; inadequate response → add biologic, often TNF inhibitor
NSAIDs relieve symptoms without preventing joint damage; glucocorticoid bridge only briefly when necessary
Methotrexate: avoid pregnancy, significant liver disease; monitor CBC, creatinine, LFTs
TNF inhibitors: avoid active infection, advanced heart failure, demyelinating disease

rows.label: Complications
items: ★ **Atlantoaxial subluxation** → cord compression; protect cervical spine during airway management
Accelerated cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, secondary amyloidosis; immunosuppression → serious infections

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, occupational/physical rehabilitation; assess bone and cardiovascular risk
Screen TB and hepatitis B before biologics; update vaccines before immunosuppression

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteoarthritis: bony DIP/first CMC enlargement, brief stiffness
Psoriatic arthritis: dactylitis, nail pitting, asymmetric or DIP involvement
SLE arthritis: usually nonerosive, rash/cytopenias, disease-specific autoantibodies

septic-arthritis.name: Septic arthritis
septic-arthritis.scope: Nongonococcal, gonococcal, prosthetic joint infection, IV drug use, empiric coverage (vancomycin + cefepime), contiguous osteomyelitis
septic-arthritis.core: Acutely painful swollen joint with restricted passive motion → urgent aspiration and drainage; delayed treatment rapidly destroys cartilage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthesis, recent surgery/injection, rheumatoid arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, bacteremia
IV drug use → S aureus and gram-negative risk, including Pseudomonas
Young sexually active adults → disseminated gonorrhea; adjacent ulcers/osteomyelitis → contiguous spread
RA joint with new febrile monoarthritis → infection until aspirated, not flare

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually acute monoarthritis, often knee; fever may be absent, especially in older/immunocompromised adults
★ **Severe pain with both active and passive motion**; inability to bear weight; child's hip held flexed, abducted, externally rotated
Gonococcal dissemination: migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules; may progress to purulent monoarthritis
Prosthetic infection: persistent pain, loosening, wound drainage or sinus tract, sometimes minimal systemic illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hematogenous seeding or direct inoculation → neutrophilic enzymes damage articular cartilage
Implant biofilm limits antibiotic eradication without surgical source control
★ **S aureus** most common, including RA-damaged joints: gram-positive cocci in clusters
Asplenia or recent pharyngitis → **streptococci**: gram-positive cocci in chains

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Arthrocentesis before antibiotics** when stable: cell count/differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Synovial WBC >50,000/µL, neutrophil predominance supports infection; lower counts or negative Gram stain never exclude
★ **Crystals do not exclude infection**; send cultures even when gout seems likely
Blood cultures; gonococcal: aspirate on **chocolate/Thayer-Martin agar** plus mucosal NAAT; MRI for suspected contiguous osteomyelitis
New warmth/effusion in OA joint → aspirate before any intra-articular steroid

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ After cultures → **IV vancomycin + cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam** for severe disease, IV drug use, gram-negative risk
Stable low-risk adult: vancomycin ± ceftriaxone based on exposure; narrow to organism/susceptibility
Sepsis → immediate antibiotics without delaying for aspiration; large joints: arthroscopic washout; **hip → operative drainage**, not serial aspiration
Persistent symptoms → repeat drainage, seek abscess/osteomyelitis; mobilize after infection controlled

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible joint destruction, avascular necrosis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia, sepsis
Prolonged antibiotics → renal injury, line complications, C difficile; prolonged immobility → stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sterile procedures, treat skin infections, injection-harm reduction
Gonorrhea: treat partners, screen other STIs, abstain until treatment completed and partners treated

rows.label: Mimics
items: Crystal arthritis: polarized crystals; infection still possible concurrently
Bursitis: localized periarticular swelling, passive joint motion relatively preserved
Reactive arthritis: sterile inflammatory arthritis after GI/GU infection
Transient synovitis (child): afebrile, bears weight, ESR <40, WBC <12,000

table.title: Special treatment branches
rows: Debridement, implant retention, prolonged pathogen-directed antibiotics

shock.name: Shock
shock.scope: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors
shock.core: Circulatory failure causing tissue hypoperfusion; normal blood pressure does not exclude early shock.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemorrhage, GI losses, MI, infection, allergen exposure, spinal injury, thromboembolism
Recent surgery, immunosuppression, indwelling devices increase occult infection risk
Procedure bleeding: thoracentesis → intercostal artery, hemothorax; splenectomy → hemoperitoneum, left shoulder pain

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, altered mentation, oliguria, cool mottled skin; distributive forms may initially feel warm
★ **Anaphylaxis**: rapid airway swelling, wheezing, hypotension; skin findings may be absent
Neurogenic: **lost sympathetic tone** → hypotension, bradycardia or no tachycardia, warm skin after spinal cord injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen delivery falls below demand → anaerobic metabolism, lactate accumulation
Distributive vasodilation → relative hypovolemia despite normal total body fluid
Warm sepsis: high output, **high mixed venous O2**; pump failure: low contractility, congestion; hypovolemia: low preload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside ultrasound**: cardiac function, pericardial fluid, RV dilation, lung sliding, volume assessment
**Serial lactate**: hypoperfusion, best predicts course and mortality; trend with capillary refill, urine output
Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP ≥65 plus lactate >2 despite volume resuscitation
CBC, chemistry, ECG, troponin; cultures if infection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway, IV access; **isotonic crystalloid** (balanced, 0.9% saline) before imaging; restrict with pulmonary congestion
★ Hemorrhage → **control bleeding + blood products** (emergency O-negative); crystalloid as bridge; no vasopressors
★ Septic shock → antibiotics within 1 hour, drainage/debridement; crystalloid 30 mL/kg within 3 hours
★ Persistent septic hypotension → **norepinephrine**, MAP ≥65; add vasopressin, then epinephrine; refractory → hydrocortisone
Pulmonary edema after fluids → stop boluses, **inotrope**; children: epinephrine preferred, older exams may expect dopamine

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, ischemic hepatitis, DIC, ARDS, bowel ischemia, multiorgan failure
Excess fluids → edema; vasopressors → digital/mesenteric ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early infection treatment, catheter hygiene, VTE prophylaxis, hemorrhage control
After anaphylaxis: trigger avoidance, epinephrine autoinjector, allergy referral

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal syncope: transient bradycardia, rapid recovery supine
Hypoglycemia: low bedside glucose, improvement with dextrose
Isolated head injury: hypertension + bradycardia (Cushing); trauma hypotension + tachycardia → assume hemorrhage

table.title: Hemodynamics and cause-directed rescue
rows: Decompress pneumothorax; drain tamponade; reperfuse PE

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.name: Stable ischemic heart disease
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.scope: Stable angina pectoris, exercise stress testing, stress echocardiography, antianginal pharmacotherapy, invasive coronary angiography indications
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.core: Predictable exertional chest pressure relieved by rest reflects myocardial oxygen supply–demand mismatch; new rest symptoms require acute coronary syndrome evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, older age, family history of premature CAD
Anemia, tachycardia, and uncontrolled blood pressure can worsen ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Substernal squeezing, arm/jaw radiation; dyspnea or exertional indigestion may be anginal equivalents
Normal resting ECG does not exclude CAD; examination often normal between episodes
★ **Crescendo symptoms, prolonged pain, rest pain**, instability → ECG/troponins and ACS pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Flow-limiting coronary atherosclerosis restricts supply when demand rises
Microvascular dysfunction can produce ischemia despite absence of obstructive epicardial disease

rows.label: Dx
items: Resting ECG, lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function; estimate clinical likelihood before choosing testing
★ Selected intermediate-risk suspected CAD → **CCTA or stress testing**, based on suitability
★ **Coronary angiography** for high-risk noninvasive findings, refractory limiting symptoms, or suspected high-risk anatomy
Stable on medical therapy, low-risk ischemia → no repeat testing or mandatory catheterization; respect informed refusal
Sedentary, risk factors, starting vigorous exercise: no routine stress test; older exam questions may expect exercise ECG

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Relief → **sublingual nitroglycerin**; avoid with recent PDE-5 inhibitor use or hypotension
★ Prevention → **aspirin + high-intensity statin**; manage BP/diabetes, lifestyle and exercise
Antianginal first-line: beta blocker or calcium-channel blocker; persistent symptoms → long-acting nitrate or ranolazine
Beta blockers improve outcomes for selected recent MI/reduced EF indications, not all stable CAD indefinitely
Refractory symptoms → revascularization; CABG improves survival in left-main/selected complex multivessel disease

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, heart failure, malignant arrhythmia, sudden death
Nitrates → headache/hypotension; combining beta blocker with verapamil/diltiazem can cause bradycardia/heart block

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, Mediterranean-style diet, habitual activity; cardiac rehabilitation when eligible
ACE inhibitor/ARB when hypertension, diabetes, CKD, or reduced EF; adherence and lipid follow-up
Drug-eluting stent → **aspirin + clopidogrel**, not anticoagulant; stable CAD 6 months; older exam questions may expect 12

rows.label: Mimics
items: GERD: meal/recumbency association, regurgitation
Aortic stenosis: exertional symptoms with systolic murmur
Costochondritis: reproducible focal chest-wall tenderness
Variant (Prinzmetal) vasospasm: rest/nocturnal pain, **transient ST elevation**, nitrate relief, normal angiography → calcium-channel blocker

table.title: Functional test selection
rows: Exercise stress echocardiography or perfusion imaging
